title: Cannoli Shells and Filling
subtitle: Crisp Sicilian pastry tubes with sweet ricotta filling
excerpt: Cannoli are the great pastry of Sicily -- thin, blistered shells deep-fried until shattering-crisp, then filled with sweetened ricotta at the last possible moment. Making them at home takes time and patience, but the gap between a fresh cannolo and a bought one is enormous. Fill them only just before serving.
sourceNotes: Cannoli originated in Sicily, with roots in the Arab confectionery traditions that shaped Sicilian food for centuries. They were originally a Carnival sweet, but are now eaten year-round across Italy and wherever Sicilian communities settled.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shells keep in an airtight tin for 3 days. Fill just before serving.

content.text: You need metal cannoli tubes for frying. Wooden dowels will scorch in hot oil -- tubes are not optional for the shell stage.

items.prepNote: 1 whole egg for the dough, 1 yolk for sealing the shells
drained overnight in a fine sieve
use 100g mascarpone for a richer filling
use 50g dark chocolate chips to stir into the filling

content.text: Make the dough: rub the butter into the flour and sugar until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add the egg and wine and mix to a smooth, firm dough. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Make the filling: beat the drained ricotta with the mascarpone (or soured cream) and honey until smooth. Stir in chocolate chips if using. Refrigerate until needed.
Roll the rested dough very thin -- about 2mm. Cut into circles roughly 10cm wide.
Wrap each circle around a metal cannoli tube. Brush one edge with egg yolk and press to seal firmly.
Heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 180C. Fry two or three shells at a time, tubes and all, for 2-3 minutes until deep golden and blistered.
Lift out with tongs. Leave to cool slightly on kitchen paper, then slide the tubes out carefully while still warm.
Just before serving, spoon or pipe the ricotta filling into both ends of each shell. Serve within 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The shells are soft rather than crisp
items.cause: The oil was not hot enough, or the shells were filled too far in advance.
items.fix: Check the oil reaches 180C before frying. Never fill shells more than 30 minutes before eating -- moisture from the filling softens them fast.

items.symptom: The shells cracked when the tube was removed
items.cause: The dough was too thick, or the shell cooled and contracted around the tube.
items.fix: Roll the dough to 2mm -- no thicker. Remove the tubes while they are still warm and slightly flexible, not after they have fully cooled.

items.symptom: The filling is wet and runs out of the shell
items.cause: The ricotta was not drained for long enough.
items.fix: Drain the ricotta in a fine sieve over a bowl in the fridge overnight. Fresh ricotta carries a lot of liquid that makes the filling loose.

content.text: Cannoli are the emblem of Sicilian pastry-making. Every town on the island has its own version, some with candied peel, some with pistachios. The best are found in small pasticcerie, filled to order. Everywhere else, they are a reminder of what Sicily does better than anywhere.
